docRequirement: mcp.md:761 — "If your MCP server uses an authentication scheme other than OAuth, such as Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO, use `headersHelper` to generate request headers at connection time. Claude Code runs the command and merges its output into the connection headers." The same section binds the mechanics: "The command must write a JSON object of string key-value pairs to stdout"; "The command runs in a shell with a 10-second timeout, from the session's current working directory"; "Dynamic headers override any static `headers` with the same name"; "The helper runs fresh on each connection, at session start and on reconnect. There is no caching"; on a tool call's `401 Unauthorized` or `403 Forbidden` Claude "automatically re-runs the helper, reconnects with the fresh headers, and retries the call once"; the helper process gets exactly `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL` and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` ("Set only when a plugin provides the server"); for a plugin-provided server the helper's working directory is the plugin root (mcp.md:809); a plugin `headersHelper` may NOT reference `${user_config.*}` and the server must be reported as misconfigured instead (mcp.md:811); and "`headersHelper` executes arbitrary shell commands. When defined at project or local scope, it only runs after you accept the workspace trust dialog" (mcp.md:814). The field is accepted on `http`, `sse` (mcp.md:765-785) and `ws` (mcp.md:147), and plugin path placeholders substitute into it (mcp.md:320).
current: There is no dynamic header generator anywhere in the fork, for any transport. The field never survives parsing, so nothing downstream could execute it even if it wanted to. (1) Type: `SdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:733-800) has no `headersHelper` member on the `'http' | 'sse'` arm, the `'ws'` arm or the `'stdio'` arm — only `headers?: Record<string, string>`. (2) Project `.mcp.json` reader: `parseProjectMcpServer` handles http/sse at packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:119-134 and never reads `raw.headersHelper`; the field is named ONLY in the `ws` arm, where :147-148 does `if (raw.headersHelper !== undefined) problems.push('"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored')`, and the docblock at :139-143 states the absence outright. `parseMcpServersDocument` (:180-216) has no generic unknown-key sweep, so an http/sse `headersHelper` is dropped with no message at all. Those `warn` strings go to the agent debug log, not a user surface — the live caller passes `message => debug(message)` (packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:461-463). (3) Claude plugin adapter: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1058 warns for every transport (`plugin.format.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported`) and files `deferred.push({ externalKind: 'mcp', reasonCode: 'plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported' })`; the server still imports, with static headers only. `PluginMcpDescriptor` (packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:168-204) carries `headers` and no helper field, and `mcpDescriptorToSdkConfig` (packages/shared/src/plugins/projection.ts:375-392) copies only `url`/`headers`. (4) Connect path: `sdkConfigToClientConfig` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:429-464) copies `url` + `headers`; `McpClientPool.connect` (:1111-1143) constructs `new NessyMcpClient(clientConfig, …)` with no header-resolution step; `NessyMcpClient`'s transports take the static record once at construction (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:401-424 — `requestInit: { headers: config.headers }` for http and sse, and `new WebSocketClientTransport(new URL(config.url))` for ws, which sends no headers at all). (5) No retry seam: `isRetryableDiscoveryError` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:112-121) deliberately excludes 4xx — "Auth errors, 4xx responses (including 401/403) … are NOT retried". (6) Environment: `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME|CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL'` over packages, apps and scripts returns hits in docs only — zero in code. (7) The absence is even asserted as an invariant: packages/shared/src/plugins/user-config-substitution.ts:25-30 reasons that no `${user_config.*}` shell-injection refusal is needed for `headersHelper` because "Nessy implements no `headersHelper` for any transport, so there is no helper command to substitute into at all", and packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/user-config-substitution.test.ts:197-213 locks that in.
divergence: The entire mechanism is absent — this is not a key-name or a value mismatch. Claude runs a shell command at each connect and merges its stdout JSON over the static headers; we parse the field off the config and connect with static headers only. Four separable deltas: (a) no executor at all — no spawn, no 10s timeout, no stdout JSON contract, no dynamic-over-static merge; (b) no helper environment — `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`/`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL`/`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` exist nowhere in code, and there is no plugin-root cwd rule; (c) no 401/403 re-run-and-retry-once; (d) the reporting we do have is itself asymmetric — the plugin path warns and files a deferred record on every transport, the `.mcp.json` path warns only on `ws`, and on `http`/`sse` (the two transports the doc's own examples use) the field is dropped in total silence, which is exactly the failure mode the code comment at project-config.ts:141-143 says the warning exists to prevent.

change.what: Add the helper to the `'http' | 'sse'` arm (:733) and the `'ws'` arm. Prefer a resolved spec over the raw string — `headersHelper?: { command: string; cwd?: string; pluginRoot?: string }` — because the doc's cwd rule differs by origin (session cwd for `.mcp.json`, plugin root for a plugin-provided server, mcp.md:793/:809) and only the materializer has the plugin root in scope. Document that the value is a shell command and never a secret (mcp.md:811 forbids `${user_config.*}` in it).

The executor. `resolveMcpDynamicHeaders(spec, { serverName, url }): Promise<Record<string,string>>` — spawn through a shell, cwd = `spec.cwd`, env = process env plus `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` only when `spec.pluginRoot` is set; hard 10 000 ms timeout with SIGTERM then SIGKILL; buffer stdout, `JSON.parse`, accept ONLY a flat object whose every value is a string, otherwise reject with a named error. Copy the spawn/timeout/kill shape from packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:717-750 rather than inventing a second one. Fail-soft contract must be decided and stated in the file: on non-zero exit, timeout or malformed stdout, connect with the static headers and log the named reason (do not throw the connect away silently).

Delete the `problems.push('"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored')` at :147-148 and its docblock at :139-143. Read `raw.headersHelper` (string only; anything else keeps a `problems` entry) in BOTH the http/sse arm (:119-134) and the ws arm (:144-161) and emit it on the config. Do NOT run it through `expand()` — mcp.md:452-458 lists the expansion locations as `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers` and does not include `headersHelper`.

Resolve in `connect` (:1111-1143), after the ws address guard and before `new NessyMcpClient`, then merge dynamic over static (`{ ...clientConfig.headers, ...dynamic }`) — mcp.md:791 "Dynamic headers override any static `headers` with the same name". It must run per connect ATTEMPT, inside the path `connectWithRetries`/`connectWithDeadline` drives, because mcp.md:795 says "The helper runs fresh on each connection, at session start and on reconnect. There is no caching" — resolving once at parse time would silently cache a short-lived token. `sdkConfigToClientConfig` (:429-464) only needs to carry the spec through if you keep resolution inside the client; keep the RESOLVED headers out of `mcpConnectionKey` (:160-163, sha256 over the config), otherwise every reconnect mints a new connection identity and the pool never recognises the server it already has.

Second, separable step (mcp.md:797): on a tool call returning 401 or 403 for a connection whose config has a `headersHelper`, re-run the helper, reconnect and retry the call exactly once; only if that retry also fails mark the server as needing authentication. Today `isRetryableDiscoveryError` (:112-121) explicitly excludes 4xx, so this is a new branch, not a threshold change — do not widen the existing retry predicate, which would start retrying permanent 4xx for every server.
Add `headersHelper?: string` beside `headers` (:203). One line; it is the persisted manifest shape, see blastRadius.

Replace the warn+deferred block at :1047-1058 with: carry `stringField(rawServer,'headersHelper')` through `rewriteClaudeTokens` (mcp.md:320 substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`/`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` into `headersHelper`), and add an ERROR diagnostic when it references `${user_config.*}` (mcp.md:811) — mirror the existing shell-form refusal at :1508-1518 (`plugin.format.claude_hook_user_config_shell_form`), same shape, new code e.g. `plugin.format.claude_mcp_headers_helper_user_config`. Bump `CLAUDE_ADAPTER_VERSION` at :144 from '1' to '2' so `migrateOutdatedPluginAdaptersOnStartup` re-normalizes already-installed Claude plugins and their persisted manifests pick the field up.
Carry `headersHelper` on the remote branch at :387-392, next to `headers`.

Carry the helper command as a server-only pinned field beside `descriptorHeaders` — add `descriptorHeadersHelper?: string` to `RuntimeMcpServer` (:299) and populate it at :1147 exactly like `descriptorHeaders`. Keep it OFF `SdkMcpServerConfigWithoutSecrets` (:205-230) unless the safe view needs to show it; the safe view carries `headerNames` rather than values for a reason, and a command string is closer to `command` (already carried for stdio) than to a header value.

At :643-660, emit `headersHelper: { command, cwd, pluginRoot }` — `pluginRoot`/`cwd` = `server.pluginRuntime.rootPath` when the server is plugin-provided (mcp.md:809), otherwise the session/workspace cwd, matching how the stdio branch already resolves cwd at :571-577. Also include the helper string in the unresolved-reference scan at :1169 so a `${VAR}` it cannot resolve is named like a header's.

The docblock's premise at :25-30 ("Nessy implements no `headersHelper` for any transport, so there is no helper command to substitute into at all") stops being true — rewrite it to point at the new adapter-side refusal. `substituteMcp` (:251-286) must keep NOT substituting into `headersHelper`: the field is shell-parsed, so the refusal is the contract (mcp.md:811, errors.md:1392 names `headers` as the safe alternative).

change.what: Invert: assert the ws arm now emits `headersHelper` on the parsed config and no longer warns. Add the http and sse cases that are missing today — that gap is why the silent http/sse drop survived.

One positive path (helper stdout `{"Authorization":"Bearer x"}` overrides a static `Authorization`, and the resolved value reaches the transport) and one negative (non-zero exit / non-JSON / non-string value → connect proceeds with static headers and the named reason is logged). Plus a second-connect assertion proving the helper re-ran rather than being cached.

blastRadius: `SdkMcpServerConfig` is the shared MCP config type: it is read by `sdkConfigToClientConfig` and `mcpConnectionKey` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:429, :160 — the sha256 connection identity, so any field added to it changes identity for servers that declare it), `BaseAgent.syncSources` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:1698, :1731-1800), pi-agent.ts:7014, claude-agent.ts, runtime-pool-servers.ts, plugins/runtime-projection.ts:92 `buildPluginMcpServerConfig`, and mcp/builtin-dp-servers.ts:214. The MCP pool lives in the HOST process (base-agent syncs it directly), so no Pi/Claude subprocess wire is crossed by the connection itself. Two boundaries ARE crossed and both are risk triggers in this repo. PERSISTENCE: `PluginMcpDescriptor` is part of `NessyPluginManifest`, which is persisted per install in the plugin registry on disk (packages/shared/src/plugins/store-v2.ts:42-69) — plugins installed before the change carry a manifest without the field until re-normalized, which is what the `CLAUDE_ADAPTER_VERSION` bump plus `migrateOutdatedPluginAdaptersOnStartup` (packages/shared/src/plugins/adapter-migration.ts:17-56) exists to drive. TRUST: a plugin MCP capability's `executableHash` is sha256 over the bundle hash and `JSON.stringify({definition,…})` (packages/shared/src/plugins/projection-candidates.ts:84-90), so once a declaring plugin's normalized descriptor gains `headersHelper`, its per-capability trust grant no longer matches and the user is asked to re-grant — for that plugin only; a plugin that declares no helper hashes byte-identically. SECURITY: this introduces a NEW arbitrary-shell-execution path at connect time. For project scope the doc's precondition is already satisfied structurally — `.mcp.json` is only read inside the `projectTrustState === 'trusted'` branch (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:995, :1067) — but that must be re-verified, not assumed, and the helper must never inherit a path that lets an untrusted project contribute one. Tests that currently assert the ABSENCE and will fail loudly: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/ws-transport.test.ts:46-57, packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/claude-mcp-ws.test.ts:82-96, packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/user-config-substitution.test.ts:197-213. The deferred reason code `plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported` reaches the renderer at install time (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/plugins.ts:155, apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/plugin-install-state.ts:19-45, PluginsPage.tsx:294) — removing it changes what that surface shows.
userImpact: An operator whose internal MCP server authenticates with Kerberos, an SSO cookie or a short-lived token — the doc's stated audience, and the normal corporate-gateway case in this fork — configures `headersHelper` and the server simply never works. Concretely: put a `.mcp.json` with `{"type":"http","url":…,"headersHelper":"/opt/bin/get-mcp-auth-headers.sh"}` in a trusted project and open a session; the helper is never executed, the connection goes out with whatever static headers exist (usually none), the server 401s, its tools never appear in the session, and NOTHING is said — no toast, no diagnostic, not even a warning line, because the http/sse arm drops the field silently and the ws arm's warning only reaches the agent debug log. The user sees a server that is configured and absent. On the imported-Claude-plugin path the outcome is the same, but there the user does get a signal: the plugin's install result lists a deferred `mcp` capability with reason `plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported`, so at least the cause is nameable. A `ws` server declaring it is worse still — the WebSocket transport sends no headers at all (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:416), so neither the static nor the dynamic set arrives.
notes: Every file and line cited above was read in this session (project-config.ts in full; claude.ts:1000-1090 and :1498-1525; backend/types.ts:697-800 and :813-821; mcp-pool.ts:100-190, :400-480, :1050-1210, :1560-1600; client.ts:1-120 and :330-430; runtime-pool-servers.ts:430-700; projection.ts:350-395; plugins/types.ts:168-210; resolver.ts:190-300 and :1120-1160; projection-candidates.ts:40-110; store-v2.ts:30-70; adapter-migration.ts:1-40; native-sources.ts:980-1070; user-config-substitution.ts:1-60 and :230-275; automations/hook-command.ts:1-80 and :717-750), and mcp.md was re-fetched with curl (1282 lines) rather than WebFetch. Two things I did NOT verify and that an implementer should settle first. (1) The fail-soft contract is a product decision the page does not settle: mcp.md says what a successful helper does and that a failed 401/403 retry marks the server as needing authentication, but not what happens when the helper itself exits non-zero or times out on the FIRST connect. This repo's `.mcp.json` reader has a strong house style — never sink a server for an optional field — so connecting with static headers plus a named log line is the consistent choice, but it is a choice. (2) I did not check whether a plugin-provided `headersHelper` must also be constrained by the plugin network/process authority that `pluginRuntime` enforces for stdio servers (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:363-368 throws `plugin-mcp-process-supervisor-required`); an http/sse plugin server carries only `pluginOrigin`, which has no root path (backend/types.ts:813-821), so spawning a helper for one is a new supervised-process question I did not resolve. One adjacent latent defect noticed while reading and NOT part of this finding: `isSdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:181-184) omits `'ws'`, so a ws config is briefly filed into `activeApiServers` in `registerClient` (:1069-1075) before `connect` (:1141-1142) corrects it — currently self-healing, but it would bite anything that reads those maps between the two writes.
